records.title: What Is This?
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: Layla asks about nearby objects, and Sami answers with the matching demonstrative.
records.source_brief_introduction: `مَا هَذَا؟ / مَا هَذِهِ؟` asks what a nearby item is, using the masculine or feminine demonstrative to match the noun.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:مَا هَذَا]]؟ for a masculine item and [[grammar:مَا هَذِهِ]]؟ for a feminine item; match the demonstrative to the noun.
records.expert_brief_introduction: The identification questions [[grammar:مَا هَذَا]]؟ and [[grammar:مَا هَذِهِ]]؟ combine interrogative مَا with a proximal demonstrative that agrees with the noun's grammatical gender.

records.title: Asking What This Is
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: Before a lesson, a pupil finds the classroom and checks a few object labels. The last label leads to the door.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `Is dit N?` to ask whether a nearby object is the named noun.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:Is dit N]]? to ask whether a nearby object is the named noun.
records.expert_brief_introduction: The polar interrogative [[grammar:Is dit N]]? places the finite copula before the demonstrative subject.

records.title: Living Here
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: At home in Utrecht, Mark reads a short first-person profile from a map exercise about someone living in Rotterdam.
records.source_brief_introduction: The pattern `Ik woon in N` states a place of residence.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:Ik woon in N]] to state a place of residence.
records.expert_brief_introduction: The residence pattern [[grammar:Ik woon in N]] combines finite [[grammar:wonen]] with an [[grammar:in]]-headed locative complement.

records.title: A Simple Daily Routine
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: Sophie is a student going through a simple day at home and school.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `Sophie + V stem-t` to describe a named third-person subject performing a present action.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:Sophie + V stem-t]] to describe a named third-person subject performing a present action.
records.expert_brief_introduction: The pattern [[grammar:Sophie + V stem-t]] presents controlled third-person singular present predicates without generalizing the full conjugation system.

records.title: Meeting the Family
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: Alex visits Sophie at home and meets her grandmother, Oma Anja.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `Wie is dat?` to ask who someone is and answer with `Dat is` plus the person's name or role.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:Wie is dat]]? to ask who someone is and answer with [[grammar:Dat is]] plus the person's name or role.
records.expert_brief_introduction: The person-identity interrogative [[grammar:Wie is dat]]? uses copular inversion, while the answer [[grammar:Dat is]] identifies the referent.

records.title: Planning a Picnic
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: Alex, Sophie, and Daan organize a picnic in the park and identify whose things are whose.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `Welke + noun` to ask which de-word item is meant, and use `noun + van mij/jou/hem/haar` to state who owns it.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:Welke + noun]] to ask which de-word item is meant, and use [[grammar:noun + van mij/jou/hem/haar]] to state who owns it.
records.expert_brief_introduction: The first pattern uses [[grammar:welke]] as an interrogative determiner with a common-gender count noun; the second expresses the possessor in a postnominal [[grammar:van]] phrase.

records.title: Organizing a Volunteer Event
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: Noor, Milan, and Sophie organize a volunteer information evening.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `Zullen we + infinitive?` to suggest a shared action and `misschien + V2 clause` to present an idea as possible.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:Zullen we + infinitive]]? to suggest a shared action and [[grammar:misschien + V2 clause]] to present an idea as possible.
records.expert_brief_introduction: The proposal question uses finite [[grammar:zullen]] with a final lexical infinitive; fronted [[grammar:misschien]] occupies the first field and triggers ordinary V2 order.

records.title: A Formal Information Request
grammar_patterns: direct formal Kunt u mij zeggen of + embedded polar clause?
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain:
Fatima volunteers for one afternoon at a municipal information desk, where Opa
Henk and Yasmin make formal requests.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `Zou u + infinitive + kunnen?` for a highly polite request and `Kunt u mij zeggen of + embedded polar clause?` for a formal indirect yes-no question.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:Zou u + infinitive + kunnen]]? for a highly polite request and [[grammar:Kunt u mij zeggen of + embedded polar clause]]? for a formal indirect yes-no question.
records.expert_brief_introduction: The first frame uses conditional [[grammar:zou]] to mitigate a formal request; the second combines a V1 matrix question with an [[grammar:of]]-introduced verb-final embedded polar clause.

records.title: A Saturday at the Library
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: Lina spends a quiet Saturday morning working at the library before going home at noon.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `il / elle + regular -er verb` to describe what he or she does; remove `-er` and add `-e` in the third-person singular.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:il / elle + regular -er verb]] to describe what he or she does; remove [[grammar:-er]] and add [[grammar:-e]] in the third-person singular.
records.expert_brief_introduction: Regular first-conjugation verbs form the third-person singular present with the stem plus orthographic [[grammar:-e]], while the subject noun phrase or clitic precedes the finite verb.

records.title: Buying Bread
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: Lina orders bread from the seller at a bakery in the morning.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `Je voudrais + noun` to request an item politely.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:Je voudrais + noun]] to request an item politely.
records.expert_brief_introduction: The polite request frame [[grammar:je voudrais + noun]] uses the conditional form of [[grammar:vouloir]] to soften the speaker's wish.

records.title: A Rainy Saturday
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: Rain changes Lina’s and Marc’s Saturday plans, so they spend the morning apart.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `ne + finite verb + pas` for standard written negation, placing the finite verb between `ne` and `pas`.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:ne + finite verb + pas]] for standard written negation, placing the finite verb between [[grammar:ne]] and [[grammar:pas]].
records.expert_brief_introduction: Standard bipartite negation places preverbal [[grammar:ne]] and postverbal [[grammar:pas]] around the finite verb, with [[grammar:n']] before a vowel sound.

records.title: Choosing Clothes
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: Lina chooses clothes for an event while Marc helps her compare the options.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `quel / quelle + noun` to ask which item is meant, matching the determiner to the noun's gender.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:quel / quelle + noun]] to ask which item is meant, matching the determiner to the noun's gender.
records.expert_brief_introduction: The interrogative determiner appears as [[grammar:quel]] before a masculine singular noun and [[grammar:quelle]] before a feminine singular noun.

records.title: A Family Visit
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: Lina, her brother, and her sister spend a family visit together at home.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `son / sa / ses + noun` to express third-person possession, choosing the form from the following noun's gender and number.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:son / sa / ses + noun]] to express third-person possession, choosing the form from the following noun's gender and number.
records.expert_brief_introduction: The possessive determiner agrees with the possessed noun: [[grammar:son]] is masculine singular, [[grammar:sa]] feminine singular, and [[grammar:ses]] plural.

records.title: Where Is the Key?
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: Mia asks first what an object is, and Jonas helps her locate two belongings.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `Wo ist + N?` to ask where one thing is.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:Wo ist + N]]? to ask where one thing is.
records.expert_brief_introduction: The locative content question [[grammar:Wo ist + N]]? places interrogative [[grammar:wo]] in the first field and finite [[grammar:ist]] in the second.

records.title: A Small Shopping Trip
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: Hannah buys food and juice before taking one small carrier bag to the park.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `einen / eine / ein + direct object` to mark masculine, feminine, and neuter indefinite direct objects.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:einen / eine / ein + direct object]] to mark masculine, feminine, and neuter indefinite direct objects.
records.expert_brief_introduction: The accusative indefinite article is [[grammar:einen]] for masculine nouns, [[grammar:eine]] for feminine nouns, and [[grammar:ein]] for neuter nouns.

records.title: Ordering at a Café
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: Mia and Jonas practise a café conversation while Jonas plays the waiter.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `ich möchte + noun / infinitive` to state politely what you would like, keeping the infinitive at the end when one is used.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:ich möchte + noun / infinitive]] to state politely what you would like, keeping the infinitive at the end when one is used.
records.expert_brief_introduction: Finite [[grammar:möchte]] occupies the verbal position, while an accompanying lexical infinitive remains clause-final.

records.title: A Busy Evening
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: Leonie and Tobias prepare dinner for the friend who is coming in the evening.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `separable prefix + finite verb` in a main clause by placing the finite verb in second position and the separated prefix at the end.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:separable prefix + finite verb]] in a main clause by placing the finite verb in second position and the separated prefix at the end.
records.expert_brief_introduction: A separable verb realizes its finite stem in [[grammar:V2]] position and its stressed prefix in the right clause bracket.

records.title: Repairing a Bicycle
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: Leonie asks Tobias to help inspect and repair a bicycle.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `können + infinitive` to express ability or possibility, conjugating `können` and placing the action infinitive at the end.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:können + infinitive]] to express ability or possibility, conjugating [[grammar:können]] and placing the action infinitive at the end.
records.expert_brief_introduction: The modal [[grammar:können]] is finite and the lexical verb remains a bare infinitive in the clause-final position.

records.title: A Rainy Bus Ride
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: Mia stays home sick while Jonas travels through the rain and later visits her for tea.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `weil + subordinate clause` to give a reason, placing the finite verb at the end of the `weil` clause.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:weil + subordinate clause]] to give a reason, placing the finite verb at the end of the [[grammar:weil]] clause.
records.expert_brief_introduction: The subordinating conjunction [[grammar:weil]] introduces a causal clause whose finite verb occupies the final position.

records.title: A Market Plan
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: Rina asks Amit politely, and they agree to buy fruit and leave at three.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `क्या आप + place + चलेंगे?` to ask politely whether someone will go somewhere.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:क्या आप + place + चलेंगे]]? to ask politely whether someone will go somewhere.
records.expert_brief_introduction: Clause-initial [[grammar:क्या]] marks a polar question, while honorific [[grammar:आप]] selects plural-honorific agreement in [[grammar:चलेंगे]].

records.title: A Monday at School
grammar_patterns: N は い-adjective です
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: 佐藤あき (Aki) notices the classroom and begins reading during a busy Monday at school.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `N は い-adjective です` to describe a topic politely, keeping the adjective's final `い` before `です`.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:N は い-adjective です]] to describe a topic politely, keeping the adjective's final [[grammar:い]] before [[grammar:です]].
records.expert_brief_introduction: An [[grammar:い-adjective]] functions directly as the predicate, while [[grammar:です]] adds politeness and the nonpast affirmative retains final [[grammar:-い]].

records.title: Talking About Likes
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: 佐藤あき (Aki) and 中村ゆき (Yuki) ask each other about everyday likes.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `N が 好きです` to say that someone likes something, marking the liked item with `が`.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:N が 好きです]] to say that someone likes something, marking the liked item with [[grammar:が]].
records.expert_brief_introduction: The liked entity is marked by [[grammar:が]], and [[grammar:好きです]] forms an adjectival predicate rather than a transitive verb phrase.

records.title: A Simple School Day
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: 佐藤あき (Aki) follows her school-day schedule from morning until night.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `time + に + verb` to state when an action happens at a specific time.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:time + に + verb]] to state when an action happens at a specific time.
records.expert_brief_introduction: Temporal [[grammar:に]] marks a specific clock time before the event predicate; broad periods may occur without it.

records.title: Ordering at a Small Shop
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: 中村ゆき (Yuki) asks 店員, an unnamed shop clerk, for three items and the total price.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `N を ください` to request an item politely, marking the requested item with `を`.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:N を ください]] to request an item politely, marking the requested item with [[grammar:を]].
records.expert_brief_introduction: The requested noun phrase takes accusative [[grammar:を]] before the polite request predicate [[grammar:ください]].

records.title: Yesterday Near the Station
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: 佐藤あき (Aki) and 中村ゆき (Yuki) spend yesterday near the station, a shop, and the park.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `verb stem + ました` for a completed polite past action, replacing the `ます` ending with `ました`.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:verb stem + ました]] for a completed polite past action, replacing the [[grammar:ます]] ending with [[grammar:ました]].
records.expert_brief_introduction: The polite past affirmative is formed by attaching [[grammar:ました]] to the continuative stem used before [[grammar:ます]].

records.title: Checking a New Classroom
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: Before a joint school-library session, 박서연 checks a new school classroom, compares the spaces, and prepares to read there.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `N이/가 descriptive-아요/어요` to describe a noun politely. Korean descriptive verbs form the predicate directly; they do not take `이에요/예요` after them.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:N이/가 descriptive-아요/어요]] to describe a noun politely without adding a copula.
records.expert_brief_introduction: A Korean descriptive verb inflects directly as the polite nonpast predicate, while nominative [[grammar:이/가]] marks the described nominal.

records.title: Buying Snacks for the Group
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: Before the reading program, 45-year-old public librarian 정수진 orders food and drinks from 점원, an unnamed shop clerk.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `N 주세요` to request an item politely. In this compact service pattern, Korean commonly omits the object particle `을/를`.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:N 주세요]] for a compact polite request. The object particle is commonly omitted.
records.expert_brief_introduction: The requested nominal precedes honorific request form [[grammar:주세요]]; service discourse licenses a bare noun, and [[grammar:N은/는요]]? forms an elliptical follow-up.

records.title: Junho's School-Day Schedule
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: On a school day that includes a library meeting, 이준호 follows a fixed schedule from waking up through returning home.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `time + 에 + verb` to say when an action happens at a specific time. The same particle can mark places or destinations, so interpret it from the kind of phrase before it.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:time + 에 + verb]] to state when an action happens.
records.expert_brief_introduction: Temporal [[grammar:에]] locates an event at a time point, while the same particle has directional and locative functions with place expressions.

records.title: Resting After a Busy Week
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: After a long week, 최도윤 asks 정수진 about the weather, tiredness, and whether she will exercise or rest.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `안 + verb / descriptive verb` for short negation. Put `안` immediately before a simple predicate; with many noun-plus-`하다` expressions, place it between the noun and `해요`, as in `운동 안 해요`.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:안 + verb / descriptive verb]] for short negation. With noun-plus-하다 activities, ordinary Korean often uses [[grammar:N 안 해요]].
records.expert_brief_introduction: Negative adverb [[grammar:안]] precedes a simple predicate; in analyzable noun-plus-하다 predicates it commonly appears between the nominal element and 하다.

records.title: Photographs for the Library Display
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: For a library display, 김민지 and 이준호 meet at a market, take photographs, buy food, and review the photographs in a nearby park.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `verb-았/었어요` for a completed action in polite past speech. The past marker combines and contracts with the verb stem, producing forms such as `갔어요`, `봤어요`, and `왔어요`.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:verb-았/었어요]] for a completed polite past action.
records.expert_brief_introduction: The past marker [[grammar:-았/었-]] combines with the polite ending and undergoes regular stem-vowel contraction in forms such as [[grammar:갔어요]], [[grammar:봤어요]], and [[grammar:왔어요]].

records.title: Checking School Things
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: Nguyễn Minh Anh is Nguyễn Gia Bảo’s older sister. They check their school things before leaving home.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `reference + có + N + không?` to ask whether someone has an item, choosing the reference word from the speakers' relationship.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:reference + có + N + không]]? to ask whether someone has an item, choosing the reference word from the speakers' relationship.
records.expert_brief_introduction: The polar possession frame places a relationship-sensitive person reference before [[grammar:có + N + không]]?, with final [[grammar:không]] marking the question.

records.title: Asking Prices at the Market
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: Nguyễn Minh Anh asks Nguyễn Thị Lan about vegetables and prices at a market stall.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `N + giá bao nhiêu?` to ask an item's price and `cho tôi + N` to request it.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:N + giá bao nhiêu]]? to ask an item's price and [[grammar:cho tôi + N]] to request it.
records.expert_brief_introduction: The price question places [[grammar:giá bao nhiêu]] after the item, while [[grammar:cho tôi + N]] forms a recipient-oriented request with a nominal complement.

records.title: Preparing Dinner
grammar_patterns: S + đã + V; S + đã + V + chưa?
records.primary_reading_opening_must_remain: Lê Hoàng Nam and Nguyễn Gia Bảo prepare ingredients and check what is already complete.
records.source_brief_introduction: Use `S + đã + V` to present a completed action and `S + đã + V + chưa?` to ask whether it is complete yet.
records.normal_brief_introduction: Use [[grammar:S + đã + V]] to present a completed action and [[grammar:S + đã + V + chưa]]? to ask whether it is complete yet.
records.expert_brief_introduction: The completive marker [[grammar:đã]] precedes the verb, while the polar frame [[grammar:đã + V + chưa]]? asks whether completion has occurred.
